kind: loop 8 preregistration (full-run data pipeline + training stage, prepare only; no training run in this session)
device: CPU-only preparation (Apple M5 MacBook Pro, py3.11.15 .venv-stage1); no training run in this session

scope.extraction_rationale: BigEarthNet-S2 extracts to roughly 0.5 TB; free disk is 81 GiB with a 40 GiB buffer, so no extraction is permitted. Every archive access in this loop is a single sequential gzip stream that keeps only the selected members in memory.
scope.numbers_recorded_by_this_loop: CPU unit-test outcomes, file hashes, measured shard bytes for one 2000-patch shard, and RSVQA-LR facts read from this repository. No training, throughput, memory, or accuracy number is recorded here.

inventory_observed.s2_completeness_method: local part sizes equal the HF tree lfs_size for both parts at commit 6055d57f855c13479bf11498cddf11f83db557c7; the two parts are the only V2 S2 files in that tree, so the set is complete. Full-part SHA256 was NOT recomputed in this loop (about 63.5 GB of hashing); the recorded lfs_sha256 values are the reference for the future Kaggle build.
inventory_observed.missing: nothing required for a 12-band train shard build; S1 and Reference_Maps parts are also present but out of scope

shard_spec.split: train only (eval tiles never enter a train shard)
shard_spec.layout: one array per band at its native GSD: B02/B03/B04/B08 (patches, 120, 120), the six 20 m bands (patches, 60, 60), B01/B09 (patches, 20, 20); no resample in the shard (amendments[2])
shard_spec.normalization: none in the shard; the frozen norm contract is applied at load time by the existing data.bigearthnet_s2 loader path
shard_spec.container: one .npz per shard (ZIP store, no deflate) holding one array per band; one sidecar .json holding the rows
shard_spec.container_rationale: per-shard random access, no per-sample decode, and no CPU cost at training time. The deflate ratio is measured on the proof shard and recorded; a compressed variant is NOT adopted in this loop and would need its own pre-registration.
shard_spec.manifest: data/manifests/bigearthnet/stage1-shards.v1.json with per-shard sha256, byte sizes, row counts, tile histogram, and the selection description
shard_spec.streaming: single sequential gzip tar pass over the two S2 parts; only selected members are decoded, through rasterio MemoryFile, never written to disk

selection.algorithm: numpy.default_rng(seed); train tiles in sorted order; patch IDs sorted within a tile; round-robin equal quotas capped by each tile's available count; no replacement; per-tile take order is that tile's rng permutation; shard order is the selection order
selection.algorithm_note: mirrors the accepted loop-4 '4000-patch-style' selection recorded in data/manifests/bigearthnet/stage1-norm-train-ids.v1.json; it is a new selection at a new seed, not a reuse of the 4,000-ID list
selection.stratification: all 48 train tiles are represented in every shard build for N >= 48; tile quotas differ by at most one patch until a tile is exhausted
selection.n_selection_rule: N is chosen as the largest value in n_grid whose measured-derived total shard bytes fit the confirmed Kaggle session disk budget. Default budget SESSION_DISK_BUDGET_BYTES = 30000000000 until the session disk is measured; the builder measures shutil.disk_usage at start and refuses to exceed the budget or to cross the 40 GiB local buffer.

split_purity.rule: every shard patch_id is in caption-geo-split.v1 train; zero eval-tile patch IDs

no_duplicates.rule: patch IDs are unique across the whole build

bands_present.rule: each shard row has all 12 bands decoded at 120x120 uint16

caption_join.rule: each shard caption is byte-identical to the type=='captioning' BigEarthNet.txt 'output' for that patch_id

native_resolution.rule: each band decodes at its native GSD (120/60/20 as measured; amendments[2])

raw_zero_fraction.rule: fraction of built patches containing any raw DN 0 (which the frozen contract rejects at normalization time)
raw_zero_fraction.on_violation: abort the build and report; patches are never silently dropped

all_one_pixel_report_only.rule: fraction of pixels where all 12 bands equal 1 is recorded, not gated (loop 3/4 already characterised it)

manifest_integrity.rule: every shard file's SHA256 and byte size in the manifest match the file on disk

determinism.rule: same seed and same N produce byte-identical per-shard SHA256 values

dataset_and_resume.loader: streaming shard reader: shard index, offset within shard, per-epoch seeded permutation, and RNG state

no_skip_no_duplicate.rule: the concatenated patch_id sequence of a kill/resume run equals the uninterrupted run exactly, element for element

continuity.rule: resumed step counter, LR, and optimizer state continue from the checkpoint without re-initialization

dataset_and_resume.epoch_behaviour: deterministic per-epoch permutation from (seed, epoch); an epoch boundary is a legal checkpoint position

train_stage.hyperparameters: identical to the accepted loop-7 plan: vision 1e-5, patch-embed 1e-4, LoRA 1e-4, r=32 alpha=64, targets q,k,v,o,gate,up,down, cosine schedule with 3% warmup, grad clip 1.0, gradient checkpointing on, fp16 + sdpa, batch size 1
train_stage.steps: parameter; set from measured samples/s so a session fits its budget, recorded in the stage JSON

wall_clock_guard.rule: at the guard the run writes a final checkpoint, flushes the results JSON, and exits cleanly with status 'wall_clock_guard_exit'; the exit is not an error and the stage records steps_completed vs steps_requested

periodic_eval.set: eval-split patches only, from a separate small shard built from the 6 eval tiles
periodic_eval.metric: mean caption-only cross-entropy on the frozen contract

train_stage.no_gates_on_learning: a full run has no pre-registered pass/fail quality gate; it records measurements only

options_to_evaluate: A: zero-fill the 9 missing bands after normalization
B: map RGB to B04/B03/B02 with a stated scale conversion and zero-fill the rest
C: map available bands by spectral match where present, zero otherwise
must_be_preregistered_before_any_rsvqa_g: chosen fill option and its exact normalization order (normalize then fill, or fill then normalize)
target pixel size and resampling for the 256x256 RSVQA-LR images
the DN/reflectance scale assumed for RSVQA-LR TIFFs (unverified locally; the files are not on this machine)
band mapping table and any scale factor, frozen before the first eval sample
that the eval-time patch embed must be the Stage-1 12-band path rather than the stock 3-channel processor path
known_risks_to_record: zero-filled bands shift the input distribution away from training on all 12 real bands
spectral confusion if an RGB band is placed in a non-RGB slot
RSVQA-LR regions and BEN countries differ, so the domain gap is not measured by any local artifact

amendments.trigger: results/stage1-loop8-shard-build-attempt1-failure.json: a selected train patch band decodes as uint16 (20, 20), not (120, 120), so attempt 1 aborted during the archive pass
amendments.change: the builder now applies explicit per-patch acceptance rules instead of aborting on the first off-size member: R1 every band must decode as 120x120 uint16; R2 all twelve bands must be present; R3 a patch containing any raw DN 0 is rejected because the frozen contract refuses to normalize such a patch; accepted patches fill shard rows in candidate order, and rejected patches are recorded with their reason and shape
amendments.candidate_pool: the candidate set is the stratified selection computed up front (select_patch_ids over the train side at the fixed seed), exactly as the accepted loop-4 selection was; only those patches are decoded, and they land in the shards in archive order
amendments.shortfall_rule: a rejected candidate is not refilled, so the accepted count can be below the selection size; the shortfall, the never-seen candidates, and every rejected patch with its reason are recorded in the manifest and the build report. Training N is the accepted count, never the requested count.

gates_added.raw_zero_fraction: unchanged at <= 0.01 over accepted patches; the fraction of candidates rejected by R3 is reported separately as candidate_rejected_fraction
gates_added.shape_rejected_recorded: every rejected patch is listed with its reason and observed shape; a rejection is never silent

amendments.gates_loosened: none. native_resolution stays a zero-violation gate over accepted patches; the previous abort-on-first-violation behaviour is replaced by an explicit, recorded rejection rule

amendments.trigger: implementation review of amendment 0: filling rows in candidate order would have to buffer every candidate decoded ahead of the head of the queue, which is unbounded for a full-train build, and accepting whatever the stream reaches first would have destroyed the tile stratification of the seeded selection
amendments.change: the selection set is computed up front and the stream keeps only those patches, so shard row order is archive order and the accepted set keeps the seeded per-tile quotas; no refilling across rejections
amendments.consequence: row order inside a shard is archive order rather than selection order; training shuffles per epoch from (seed, epoch), so row order has no effect on the training sequence

amendments.trigger: results/stage1-loop8-shard-build-attempt2-failure.json: with a uniform 120x120 acceptance rule every selected patch was rejected. Read-only diagnostics over the archive (no writes) measured the real band geometry: the 10 m bands (B02, B03, B04, B08) are 120x120, the 20 m bands (B05, B06, B07, B8A, B11, B12) are 60x60, and the 60 m bands (B01, B09) are 20x20. This is the same fact loop 3 recorded as 'B01/B09 retain visibly coarse 60 m texture after 6x bilinear upsampling'.
amendments.change: the shard stores each band at its own native GSD (uint16, no resample, no normalization), which is what 'native-res uint16 per band' means for this dataset; the frozen contract's rasterio bilinear upsampling to 120x120 and the per-band mean/std are applied at load time through data.bigearthnet_s2.apply_contract, the same path the extracted-directory loader uses. R1 becomes 'every band decodes at its documented native size (120/60/20)'. Correction: the first pass of this amendment put B08 among the 20 m bands; a diagnostic build then rejected every patch with 'shape:B08:120x120'. Sentinel-2 B08 is a 10 m band and is now grouped with B02/B03/B04. The correction was measured from the archive, not assumed.
amendments.verification: data/test_bigearthnet_shards.py::test_shard_pixels_match_the_extracted_directory_loader asserts that a shard row and the equivalent extracted TIFF directory produce identical contract-normalized tensors, so the shard path cannot drift from the frozen loader
amendments.byte_model_change: one patch is now 4x120x120x2 + 6x60x60x2 + 2x20x20x2 = 160000 bytes instead of 12x120x120x2 = 345600 bytes; all size figures and projections must come from the newly measured shard
amendments.report_only_change: the loop-3 'all twelve bands equal 1' pixel metric is not computable across native GSDs without resampling; per-band DN-1 fractions are recorded instead and remain ungated
amendments.gates_loosened: none. native_resolution is still a zero-violation gate, now defined per band's native size; the raw DN 0 rejection rule is unchanged

tests_planned.new: data/test_bigearthnet_shards.py and scripts/test_stage1_full.py (CPU, mocked model, no archive access)
